rubric.why: Scientific notation requires a number from 1 up to, but not including, 10 multiplied by a power of 10.
rubric.description: Defines the required form of scientific notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a number is written as a value from 1 to less than 10 multiplied by a power of 10.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly written scientific-notation example.

modelAnswer: Scientific notation expresses a number as the product of a number from 1 up to, but not including, 10 and an integral power of 10.

items.followUp: Define a vector quantity and give one example.

rubric.why: Magnitude alone is the defining feature of a scalar quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a scalar quantity has magnitude only.

rubric.why: A vector requires both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.

items.followUp: Can a body moving with constant velocity have acceleration? Give a reason.

rubric.why: A body moving at constant speed can still accelerate when its direction changes.
rubric.description: States that constant speed can occur with acceleration.

rubric.why: In circular motion, velocity changes because its direction changes, even if speed stays constant.
rubric.description: Explains the reason using change of direction or circular motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the direction changes, for example in circular motion.

modelAnswer: Yes, a body moving at constant speed can have acceleration.
When it moves in a circular path, its direction changes continuously, so its velocity changes and it is accelerated.

items.followUp: State two methods of increasing friction.

rubric.why: Lubricants and rolling elements reduce direct contact and therefore reduce friction.
rubric.description: Gives one valid method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid method, such as lubrication or using ball bearings.

rubric.why: Smoothing surfaces or streamlining reduces friction or resistance.
rubric.description: Gives another valid method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid method, such as polishing surfaces or streamlining.

modelAnswer: Friction can be reduced by applying lubricants, such as oil or grease, between surfaces.
It can also be reduced by using ball bearings or rollers, polishing surfaces, or streamlining a body moving through a fluid.

items.followUp: Write the equation for centripetal force and identify its symbols.

rubric.why: This is the equation for the magnitude of centripetal force.
rubric.description: Writes the correct equation for centripetal force.

rubric.why: Centripetal force is directed towards the centre of the circular path.
rubric.description: States the direction of centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force acts towards the centre of the circular path.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force that keeps a body moving in a circular path and acts towards the centre of the circle.

items.followUp: Define torque and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Torque is the turning effect of a force and depends on the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: Defines torque in terms of force and perpendicular distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing torque as the turning effect of a force, or giving torque as force multiplied by perpendicular distance from the pivot.

rubric.why: The SI unit of torque is the newton metre.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing N m or newton metre.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot; it is equal to the force multiplied by its perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Its SI unit is the newton metre (N m).

items.followUp: What is meant by the centre of gravity of a body?

rubric.why: The centre of gravity is treated as a particular point in a body.
rubric.description: Identifies the centre of gravity as a point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a point in the body.

rubric.why: The body's entire weight is considered to act at its centre of gravity.
rubric.description: States that the body's weight acts at that point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the whole weight of the body acts there.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which the whole weight of the body may be considered to act.

items.followUp: Write the value of gravitational acceleration near the Earth's surface and its SI unit.

rubric.why: The standard value of gravitational acceleration near the Earth's surface is approximately 9.8.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 9.8 or an appropriately rounded value such as 9.81.

rubric.why: Gravitational acceleration is measured in metres per second squared.

modelAnswer: The value of gravitational acceleration near the Earth's surface is g = 9.8 m/s².
